abstention.statement: There is insufficient evidence to connect the remaining 14 genes to psoriasis through a shared causal mechanism. Notably, ZBP1 has been explicitly investigated in the context of psoriasis but was shown to act independently of the PANoptosis cell death mechanism observed in psoriatic keratinocytes (PMID:PPR1233591). While Open Targets assigns a weak genetic association score to SP100 (OT:SP100-MONDO_0005083), the GWAS Catalog confirms no significant variants link this gene to the disease (GWAS:SP100:no-association). Furthermore, baseline expression data reveals that IFNW1 is not detected in normal human tissues (HPA:ENSG00000177047), and single-cell cohorts comparing normal to psoriatic skin are currently absent, preventing contextual expression analysis (CXG:MONDO_0005083:no-cohort). Highly tractable targets in this list, such as KHK, lack active compounds with known mechanisms in ChEMBL (CHEMBL:no-mechanism-KHK). Without meaningful protein-protein interactions or functional evidence linking them to the disease pathophysiology, no falsifiable causal chain can be constructed for these genes.
abstention.what_would_change_this: Robust genetic association signals linking these genes to psoriasis risk, or primary literature demonstrating a shared functional role in skin inflammation—such as an experiment showing that their perturbation alters IL-23/Th17 or interferon signaling in keratinocytes or skin-infiltrating immune cells.

object.label: mRNA Editing: A to I Conversion

subject.label: mRNA Editing: A to I Conversion

falsification.description: Knockdown of ADAR in primary human keratinocytes or neutrophils, followed by measurement of interferon signaling activation and dsRNA accumulation.

hypotheses.mechanism: Loss-of-function variants in ADAR impair A-to-I mRNA editing, a process essential for resolving endogenous double-stranded RNAs. The failure to edit these transcripts results in their accumulation, which triggers innate immune sensors and aberrantly activates interferon signaling. This chronic interferon overproduction promotes skin inflammation and defines a newly recognized interferon-dependent subtype of psoriasis.
hypotheses.title: ADAR loss-of-function drives an interferon-dependent psoriasis subtype
